bull_bear.body: 100% capex funded by internal accruals; no debt used; prioritizing capacity expansion over buybacks/dividends; sustainability investments (solar, recycling) embedded in capex
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical raw material disruption (mitigated by JG’s supplier dominance); ceramic market adoption speed; zinc price volatility (absorbed via FIFO inventory); execution delay in Dahej Phase 1
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly bullish; confident in demand sustainability; frames crises as competitive differentiators; emphasizes customer intimacy, scale, and ESG alignment; tone on recycled rubber project is 'gung-ho'
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: JG’s IATF/WHO certifications are de facto barriers to entry — no global competitor matches this; Dahej’s proximity to ceramic hub (Morbi) is a strategic play to capture unpenetrated $1B+ market; recycled rubber project could become a $500cr+ revenue stream by FY30; inventory gains are retained, not passed on — a hidden margin accelerator
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The Rs. 100 Cr Dahej project is stated to be 100% funded through internal accruals.
- Essentially debt-free balance sheet: non-current borrowings fell from INR 36 Mn (FY24) to nil in FY25 and FY26; current borrowings were INR 102 Mn (FY24), INR 1 Mn (FY25) and INR 64 Mn (FY26), against total liabilities of just INR 282 Mn in FY26.
- Balance sheet carries substantial liquidity: FY26 current investments INR 1,219 Mn (up from INR 390 Mn in FY25), cash and cash equivalents INR 162 Mn and other bank balances INR 222 Mn.
- Working capital is acknowledged as structurally heavy — 'High Working Capital' is listed among Key Strengths as a barrier; FY26 inventories were INR 918 Mn and trade receivables INR 1,710 Mn.
- Equity grew from INR 4,055 Mn (FY24) to INR 4,746 Mn (FY25) to INR 5,411 Mn (FY26); the deck discloses no dividend or buyback policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Zinc oxide: 77% utilization (can scale to 87%); Zinc sulphate: 60% utilization; Export mix: 10-15%; Non-rubber demand: ceramics (targeted via Dahej), pharma, electronics, agri; Dahej product mix: 30-35% ceramics, 30-35% tire, rest non-rubber
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Incorporated in 1975 starting with a ~600 MTPA plant in Kolkata, JGCL is described as the largest manufacturer of Zinc Oxide in India with ~31% market share (as on March 30, 2025), amongst the top 5 manufacturers globally and the largest in Asia (deck footnote: 'Excluding China').
- Described as the largest zinc recycling company, with strong R&D and in-house developed recycling technology for various forms of zinc waste/scrap; it serves 200+ domestic customers and 50+ global customers in more than 10 countries with 90%+ repeat customers.
- Tyre-customer reach is stated two ways in the deck: one slide says '9/10 Global tyre manufacturers served' and 'Top 15 Indian tyre manufacturers served', while the Key Strengths slide says '9 out of Top 10 global and Top 11 domestic Tyre manufacturers are our customers'.
- High entry barriers claimed on three fronts: large tyre accounts take on average 4-5 years minimum to approve a new vendor; a global zinc-scrap sourcing network takes decades of relationships to build; and licences (IATF, WHO GMP, US/British/European Pharma, Indian Pharmacopeia) require stringent systems and capex.
- 'No China Threat' — the deck argues zinc oxide prices are determined by zinc prices on the LME, so China has no competitive edge exporting to India. Over 95% of sales are direct to end customers.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Tyre industry capex] Per recent ATMA reports cited in the deck, an estimated capex of about INR 25,000 crore has been announced by Indian tyre majors, with approx. 25% of tyres produced in India now exported.
- [Auto demand] Per ATMA, Q1 FY27 saw volume growth across major vehicle categories: PV +26.6% YoY, 2W +16.58% YoY, CV +16.48% YoY, 3W +11.32% YoY.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 70.99%, Public 22.79%, FII 3.21%, AIF 2.11%, DII 0.89%; marquee shareholders listed are Massachusetts Institute of Technology 2.62%, Carnelian Structural Shift Fund 1.69%, CTL Trusteeship Limited 1.24% and SBI General Insurance Company Limited 0.89%.
- [Future strategy] Stated growth strategies are: expand product portfolio, deeper penetration in domestic markets, diversify customer applications in end-user industries, ramp-up of the zinc sulphate business, and expansion to new geographies.
- [Geography] Geographical presence listed as India, Australia, other SAARC countries, Thailand and Europe, with a slide annotation reading 'Constitutes 99.25% of total exports from India' whose subject is ambiguous in the extract.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin 9.4% in Q4 suppressed by March energy cost spike (doubled) and spot zinc dross procurement (LME surge); pricing fully passed on from April 1, 2026; inventory gains from Q3-Q1 zinc price rise partially offset by March cost shock; baseline margin 10-11%, target 13-14% with premium grades
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: double-digit volume growth expected in FY27; margin: 10-11% baseline, targeting 13-14% with higher-value products; order inflow: strong visibility from tire capex (INR20,000cr over 3 yrs); capex/commissioning: Dahej Phase 1 commissioning H1FY27, brownfield debottlenecking at Naidupeta by Dec26, total capex INR100cr from internal accruals
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Recycled rubber intermediates (pilot validated, commercial project in pipeline); ceramic market entry via Dahej (near Morbi hub); non-rubber share expansion (targeting 30%+ of revenue); potential eastern capacity expansion
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: JG Chemicals delivered record FY26 financials driven by robust tire demand and GST-led auto revival, with Dahej capacity expansion and recycled rubber R&D creating multi-year growth visibility; margin resilience despite March raw material spikes confirms pricing power and supply chain dominance, positioning JG as the indispensable zinc solutions partner for global tire and emerging ceramic markets.
